name: cross-engine-validation
title: Cross-engine validation: do tellurium, COPASI and the native process agree?
question:
Run the same model (Teusink glycolysis, BIOMD0000000064) monolithically in all
three engines this investigation uses — tellurium (libroadrunner/CVODE), COPASI,
and the hand-ported native process — and ask: do they agree on the trajectory,
and how does that engine-agreement compare to the error the decomposition
*split* itself introduces?
hypothesis:
The three engines solve the same ODEs, so their monolithic trajectories should
agree to numerical tolerance (far below any decomposition splitting error). If
so, cross-engine disagreement is NOT a source of the decomposition cost — the
additive split is — which is the point a reviewer needs to trust the other
decomposition studies. COPASI is not bit-reproducible, so its agreement is a
tolerance, not an identity.
objective:
Measure, per engine, the max relative error of its monolithic glycolysis run
against the tellurium reference, graded against a tolerance; and report the
decomposition additive-split error as a first-class metric alongside it, so the
two sources of error (engine vs split) are directly comparable.
description:
Validation study for the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis
(17 floating species). The cross-engine agreement harness
(viva_sbml_decomposition.harness.cross_engine) runs the model in each engine —
COPASI through the retrying subprocess that survives its ~1-in-6 loader abort,
the native process being a glycolysis-specific hand-ported RHS — and compares
each trajectory to the tellurium reference with the accuracy harness.

First-class splitting-error context: the additive (Jacobi) decomposition split
measured in `mechanical-split-cost` costs a first-order error that shrinks with
the coupling interval (max relative error 0.857 at interval 0.1 -> 0.112 at
0.0125 -> 0.0066 at 0.001). Cross-engine disagreement, by contrast, is ~1e-7 —
four to six orders of magnitude smaller. The engines agree; the split is the
cost. This study makes that comparison explicit for the reviewer.

expected_behavior.name: engines-agree-on-the-same-model
expected_behavior.observable: max relative error of each engine's monolithic glycolysis run vs the tellurium reference
expected_behavior.condition: every engine that runs agrees with tellurium to < 1e-3 (measured ~1e-7); COPASI not bit-reproducible, aborts tolerated
expected_behavior.rationale: the three engines solve the same ODEs, so monolithic disagreement must be numerical-tolerance small — otherwise the other studies' engine choices would be confounded.

readouts.name: cross_engine_max_rel_err
readouts.description: Per-engine max relative error of the monolithic glycolysis trajectory vs the tellurium reference.
